title: Park centered and close enough for the cable
bullets: Align with the stall and center in the space
Avoid stretching the cable across another stall
Leave space for neighboring doors to open safely
why: Keeps stalls usable and reduces cable wear.

title: Choose a stall that fits your charge port location
bullets: Pick the stall that allows a clean cable path to your port
Avoid occupying a second stall just to make the cable reach
why: Prevents blocking and cable strain.

title: Never take two stalls (even briefly)
bullets: If alignment is hard, reposition instead of straddling lines
If the site is tight, ask a nearby driver for space rather than blocking
why: A single car can halve station capacity.

title: If you’re troubleshooting, pull aside quickly
bullets: Try once, then move to another stall if it fails
If you need app/account steps, pull into regular parking first
why: Keeps stalls available for charging cars.

title: Respect the local queue flow
bullets: If there’s an obvious line, join it instead of jumping to an open stall
If unsure, ask politely: “Is there a queue?”
why: Avoids conflict and keeps things fair.

title: Watch for pedestrians and tight turning angles
bullets: People walk between cars and cables
Back in/out slowly and use signals
why: Charging areas can be crowded and chaotic.

title: Don’t block the drive lane while waiting
bullets: If stalls are full, stage in a normal spot (if safe)
Leave room for cars to enter/exit stalls
why: Prevents gridlock and keeps access clear.

title: Keep trunk/door access from spilling into neighboring stalls
bullets: Load/unload quickly if others are waiting
Avoid leaving doors wide open next to a charging neighbor
why: Reduces accidental door dings and bottlenecks.

title: Don’t leave carts by stalls
bullets: Return carts to corrals
Keep the stall area clear of obstacles
why: Prevents blocked access and damage.

title: Stay reachable if it’s crowded
bullets: Keep notifications on
Be ready to move when you’re near your target
why: Turnover matters most at busy stations.

title: Don’t unplug someone else’s car
bullets: Even if it looks finished, don’t touch their connector
If there’s an issue, notify site staff or the driver
why: Consent and safety — and avoids confrontation.

title: Keep volume reasonable (especially at night)
bullets: Headphones if you’re watching videos
Avoid loud phone calls near others’ open windows
why: Shared spaces get stressful fast.

title: Keep the area tidy
bullets: Don’t leave trash around stalls
If you see a small mess, consider tossing it
why: Better sites stay open and maintained.

title: Handle connectors gently
bullets: Don’t drop connectors onto pavement
Avoid yanking or twisting the cable
why: Less wear means fewer broken stalls.

title: Keep the connector off the ground when possible
bullets: Don’t drag the connector across dirt/gravel
If it falls, check for debris before re-seating
why: Debris can cause poor connections and errors.

title: Avoid charging to very high % when others are waiting
bullets: Charge enough to comfortably reach your next stop + buffer
High SoC charging is slower and ties up a stall longer
why: This is the biggest throughput killer at busy sites.

title: If you step away, leave yourself a clear return reminder
bullets: Set a timer for 5–10 minutes before your target
Avoid ‘I’ll check later’ when a queue is forming
why: Prevents accidental overstays.

title: Don’t route the cable through another stall’s space
bullets: Keep the cable within your stall footprint
If the layout forces awkward routing, choose another stall
why: Neighbors need safe access too.

title: Be patient with new EV drivers
bullets: Offer quick help if asked
Keep it short and friendly (they may be stressed)
why: Good stations are built on good behavior.

title: Move promptly when you’re finished
bullets: If you hit your target, go — don’t linger
Don’t treat a full stall as parking while you shop
why: One slow mover can create a line.

title: Charge only what you need
bullets: Prioritize getting to the next stop efficiently
Let others get in if they’re waiting
why: Faster turnover helps everyone.

title: Don’t park in a charging stall unless you’re charging
bullets: If you’re not plugging in, use regular parking
If you’re waiting, stage elsewhere safely
why: Blocking stalls is the fastest way to escalate tension.

title: Communicate clearly if there’s a queue
bullets: Make eye contact and use a friendly wave
If you’re next, pull forward promptly but safely
why: Reduces confusion and disputes.

title: Don’t cut the line — even if a stall opens
bullets: If people are waiting in order, respect that order
If the system is unclear, ask rather than assume
why: Fairness prevents drama.

title: If a stall is dead/slow, tell the next driver politely
bullets: A quick: “That one failed for me” is enough
Don’t lecture — just inform
why: Saves time and keeps the line moving.

title: Keep food/restroom runs brief if people are waiting
bullets: If you need a longer stop, consider leaving and returning later
Avoid disappearing near your finish time
why: Queues form quickly when people vanish.

title: Don’t block stalls for photos or content
bullets: If you want pictures, pull to a normal spot
Keep charging lanes clear
why: Stations aren’t photo sets when lines exist.

title: Avoid unnecessary re-plugging or stall-hopping
bullets: If you’re charging normally, don’t switch stalls for minor gains
Switch only if there’s an actual problem
why: Unnecessary churn confuses queues and wastes time.

title: Return the connector properly
bullets: Seat the connector back in its holster
Don’t drop it or leave it dangling
why: Helps keep equipment reliable.

title: Do a quick trash check before you leave
bullets: Take cups/wrappers with you
Don’t leave wipes or paper towels near stalls
why: Clean sites get fewer restrictions and closures.

title: Unplug and depart without blocking others
bullets: Unplug, stow, and go
If you need to set navigation, pull into regular parking
why: Keeps exits clear for the next driver.

title: Leave the stall ready for the next person
bullets: Avoid leaving the cable stretched or twisted
If the connector is visibly dirty, gently knock off debris (no liquids)
why: The next driver shouldn’t inherit a problem.

title: Report major issues without blocking a stall
bullets: If you need to contact support, move to a normal spot first
Log the stall number/time for your own records
why: Support calls can take time — keep stalls flowing.

title: Avoid confrontation — assume confusion first
bullets: If someone makes a mistake, keep it calm
Ask a simple question before accusing
why: Stations can be stressful; calm keeps everyone safe.

title: Keep kids and pets close
bullets: Charging lanes have moving cars and cables
Don’t let children run between stalls
why: Safety risk is highest in tight parking rows.

title: Don’t create trip hazards with cables or gear
bullets: Keep personal items out of walk paths
Avoid letting cable loops sit where people step
why: Trips and falls happen fast in crowded lots.

title: At night, avoid shining bright lights into other cars
bullets: Turn down interior brightness if you’re parked close
Avoid high beams while maneuvering near stalls
why: Glare increases stress and reduces visibility.

title: Don’t smoke/vape near charging equipment
bullets: Step away from stalls if you smoke
Dispose of butts safely (never on the ground)
why: It’s inconsiderate and can be a safety issue.

title: Keep music private
bullets: No loud speakers between cars
Use headphones if you’re outside the vehicle
why: People are often tired and traveling.

title: If asked, give short, helpful answers
bullets: “Queue starts there” / “That stall failed for me”
Avoid lecturing or gatekeeping
why: Keeps the vibe friendly and the line moving.

title: Don’t idle in a stall while deciding what to do
bullets: If you’re unsure about charging, pull into normal parking to decide
Only occupy a stall when you’re ready to plug in
why: Stalls are for charging, not staging.

title: Keep car cleaning brief if others are waiting
bullets: A quick windshield wipe is fine
Don’t treat the stall as a detailing bay
why: People notice stall time, not your intent.

title: If you truly need 100%, aim for off-peak hours
bullets: Charging to 100% takes longer near the top
If the station is packed, consider a shorter stop now and another later
why: Maximizes fairness and your own time efficiency.

title: Set your route after you leave the stall
bullets: If you need to compare chargers or plan stops, pull into a normal spot
Don’t block exits while typing
why: Stops small delays from cascading into a queue.

title: Don’t discard food or liquids under stalls
bullets: Spills attract pests and create slip hazards
Dispose of liquids in appropriate drains/trash
why: Keeps the site cleaner and safer.

title: Leave access clear for anyone who needs extra space
bullets: Don’t crowd accessible pathways
Avoid blocking curb cuts or ramps
why: Access matters more than convenience.

title: Be mindful of door dings
bullets: Open doors slowly in tight stalls
If you have passengers, guide them
why: Charging sites pack cars close together.

title: Don’t hold a stall for a friend
bullets: If there’s a queue, the next car in line gets the next stall
Meeting up is fine — holding capacity isn’t
why: Queues only work when everyone follows them.

title: Before you exit, make sure you’re not blocking a neighbor’s path
bullets: Let others back out if they’re signaling
Yield in tight aisles
why: Prevents small jams that snowball into queues.

title: Avoid open flames near stalls
bullets: No grilling/candles near charging equipment
Keep any heat sources well away from cables
why: It’s rare, but the risk is needless.

title: Do a quick stall signage check
bullets: Some stalls are reserved, offline, or differently rated
Respect posted rules at shared lots
why: Prevents avoidable friction and confusion.

title: Don’t block trash bins or access paths
bullets: People need to walk through the area
Keep the space functional
why: Small blocks create big annoyances.

title: If there’s a host/attendant, follow their direction
bullets: They may be managing stalls for flow
Ask short questions and comply
why: A managed queue is faster than chaos.

title: If you hit an end-of-session error, clear the stall first
bullets: Move to normal parking, then handle app/payment issues
Note the stall ID and time
why: Keep stalls available while you resolve admin issues.

title: Keep unsolicited advice minimal
bullets: Offer help only if someone looks stuck or asks
A quick tip beats a lecture
why: People are tired and traveling — keep it friendly.
